name: Lena Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I teach beginner keyboard on Thursdays, play the organ for Sunday services and write simple choir arrangements when asked. I have a bachelor’s degree in music and years at the bench, but this town pays modestly and there are few other organ posts.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What makes the work worth doing, and what wears you down?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: When the room sings in time with the organ, the work feels right. Late service fees wear me down because the mortgage never sends a polite delay note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chapel committee that a faster list of service dates is useful, but someone still has to play the organ when people sing. I would keep the Sunday services and Thursday pupils.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage already makes me watch every paid service. My partner’s delivery hours are uneven, and we have about three weeks of expenses saved despite my years of playing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the Sunday organ bench and my Thursday beginner keyboard lessons this winter. I would ask the committee for the next quarter’s paid rota before agreeing to extra school costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about money now. A small software change does not give the household another week of savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened when a service fee arrived late?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month a memorial service moved, and the fee came a week late. We delayed replacing the children’s winter shoes until it arrived.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does your degree change about your work now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a music bachelor’s and know how to support a congregation, but the pay here is modest. A degree does not pay the mortgage on a late-fee week.

I would ask for a **paid Sunday rota** in advance.
think: Our **three-week cushion** and uneven delivery hours make a late fee serious.
My **music degree** does not raise the pay for this local organ bench.
do: Keep **Sunday services** and Thursday keyboard pupils this winter.
Ask the committee for the **paid quarter rota** before extra school spending.
feel: I feel **anxious** because current bills already press on the household.
S0.quote: A degree does not pay the mortgage on a late-fee week.
fieldNote: Her **experienced organ playing** still brings modest local pay and less than a month of savings.
The late **memorial fee** made the family delay children’s winter shoes.

steps.text: Keep Sunday organ services and Thursday beginner keyboard pupils
Delay extra school spending until paid service rota is confirmed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chapel that AI can draft bulletins, plan services and make backing music, but the organist needs a written fee. I would ask the committee to show the paid service count for spring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The short arrangements I make for community choirs may lose buyers. Generated chapel accompaniment could also replace my paid bench. My partner’s delivery pay cannot carry the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would take my last six service invoices to the committee and ask for a written spring count. If the count falls in the first year, I would drop our paid family streaming service and ask the music school about a paid evening keyboard block only if it does not clash with the children’s pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about the arrangements and possible service cuts. I know the work, but there are not many other organ benches nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which household cost would go first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The streaming service is 18 a month. It is the first easy cut, before the children’s school bus passes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the school block worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not teach the evening block if the school expects unpaid preparation. My partner can cover pickup on two evenings, so it must be one of those.

say: I would ask for a **written spring count** of paid services.
I would say a **live organist** still needs a clear fee.
think: My **choir arrangements** may lose buyers as thinking AI spreads.
Generated **chapel accompaniment** could put my regular service pay at risk.
do: Bring six **service invoices** to the committee next month.
Cancel the **18 streaming service** if paid chapel services fall.
Ask for a **paid school block** only if preparation is paid and child pickup fits.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my own fees and few nearby organ jobs.
S1.quote: My partner’s delivery pay cannot carry the mortgage alone.
fieldNote: The possible **service cut** threatens regular household income, not only a small side fee.
The evening block needs **paid preparation** and pickup fit, which narrow the school fallback.

steps.text: Keep Thursday keyboard pupils while checking written chapel service count
Cancel 18 monthly streaming service if chapel service pay falls
Ask music school about paid evening block only with preparation pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the committee that AGI by 2028 may write music and plan services cheaply, but a live congregation still needs someone to follow. I would ask for next year’s organ dates in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my arrangements to stop selling in 2028, and I think the chapel may cut the paid bench before robots play hands-on parts around 2031. Three weeks saved will not cover a long search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I would request written organ dates and ask the music school if its posted keyboard tutor vacancy is still open. If 2028 AGI cuts the chapel fee, I would apply only if the post pays for preparation and fits child pickup, and call the mortgage lender before we miss a payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed because I expect regular paid work to shrink. The mortgage date will not wait while I explain my experience to another committee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if that keyboard tutor post is filled?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep Thursday pupils until a school contract is signed. If the post is already filled, I would ask the chapel for a shorter paid rota rather than plan around a vacancy that is gone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you judge a school offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner can cover pickup on two evenings, not every night. I would take a written net offer only if the hours and travel leave more than the lost chapel fee.

say: I would demand **written organ dates** before next year’s services.
I would defend a **paid live bench** for the congregation.
think: My **arrangement sales** likely end in 2028 before 2031 playing robots.
I expect **chapel pay** to shrink before robots reach the organ.
do: Request **written chapel dates** and check posted school vacancy tomorrow.
Apply for **paid tutor post** after 2028 chapel cuts only with preparation pay, pickup fit and higher net pay.
Call the **mortgage lender** before a missed payment if chapel fees fall.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about expected regular fee loss and a three-week cushion.
S2.quote: The mortgage date will not wait while I explain my experience to another committee.
fieldNote: She expects **2028 thinking losses** and chapel cuts before 2031 playing robots.
The school route needs a **posted paid vacancy**, paid preparation, pickup and better written net pay.

steps.text: Apply for posted tutor job after 2028 chapel cuts if preparation is paid
Call mortgage lender before missing payment if chapel fees fall
Keep Thursday keyboard pupils until school contract is signed
Accept tutor post only if pickup fits and written net pay exceeds chapel fees

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the chapel that AGI by 2031 gives us five years to train a younger organist for the services. I would ask the committee to pay that person during an apprenticeship.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think arrangements go in 2031, but I might have enough keyboard pupils by then to replace some fees. Robots around 2034 could play the organ, though a congregation may prefer a person who hears its singing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This autumn I would ask the chapel to fund two paid shadowing Sundays for a younger player if the committee can cover the extra fee. In the first year after 2031 I would keep my own paid bench while the chapel books it and add a school keyboard block only with paid preparation and pickup covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious. A few years let me teach another player, but they do not erase this month’s mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What work would the apprentice actually do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would have the trainee turn pages and lead one verse while I listen. If there is no apprentice fee, I will teach my own pupils instead of asking a younger player to work free.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the school block pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school block must bring a written net fee above the childcare and travel cost. A school block without pay for preparation and childcare would make me buy a second job.

say: I would ask the chapel for **paid apprentice Sundays**.
I would tell the congregation that **live listening** matters through 2034.
think: My **arrangement sales** may end in 2031 before 2034 organ robots.
More **keyboard pupils** could replace fees if they keep booking.
do: Ask chapel to fund **two shadowing Sundays** this autumn only if fee is covered.
Keep **organ work** after 2031; add school block only with paid preparation, pickup and written fee exceeding childcare and travel.
feel: I feel **anxious** because apprenticeship does not pay this month’s mortgage.
S3.quote: A school block without pay for preparation and childcare would make me buy a second job.
fieldNote: She will not call **unpaid shadowing** an apprenticeship, matching her practical family outlook.
A second teaching block needs **written net pay** after childcare and travel plus paid preparation.

steps.text: Ask chapel for two paid shadowing Sundays only if committee funds extra fee
Keep paid organ bench after 2031 while chapel books services
Add school block only with paid preparation, pickup and written fee above travel and childcare

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children that AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to learn useful work and keep a good ear. I would still play paid services as long as the chapel asks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 I might have enough pupils to replace arrangements, but it depends on actual paid terms. Robots around 2039 might play the organ, yet our mortgage has to be covered long before then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I would put spare lesson fees into a separate account after the mortgage and food clear. In the first year after 2036 I would compare paid chapel and school hours, and apply for an open music-school tutor post only if both shrink and the written net pay after travel and childcare is higher.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feel anxious because the family still has only three weeks saved now. Ten years offers time to build savings, not a payment for this winter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you save a lesson fee every month?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some months there will be no spare lesson fee. I would not borrow to make the savings account look healthy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children about craft and pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my children to learn a craft and to expect fair pay for it. Playing well matters, but the bill still arrives on time.

say: I would tell my children to **learn a craft** and seek fair pay.
I would keep **paid chapel services** while the bench remains.
think: Paid **keyboard pupils** might replace arrangement fees before 2036.
The **mortgage** remains urgent long before possible 2039 robots.
do: Save **spare lesson fees** after mortgage and food starting this year.
Apply for **open tutor post** after 2036 only if both incomes fall, pickup fits and net pay after travel and childcare improves.
feel: I feel **anxious** because a decade does not fill today’s savings gap.
S4.quote: Ten years offers time to build savings, not a payment for this winter.
fieldNote: Her savings plan uses **genuinely spare lesson fees** after essentials, never borrowed money.
The later tutor move requires a **real vacancy** and paid time with higher written net pay.

steps.text: Save spare lesson fees after mortgage and food are paid
Apply for open tutor post if 2036 chapel and school pay fall and pickup fits
Keep paid chapel services while chapel continues booking organist

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because arrangements and chapel fees could fall before I secure school hours. Written chapel dates, a suitable paid tutor opening and early lender help would protect the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who teaches the next organist when the chapel wants the music for free. A young player cannot learn a paid craft from an empty bench.

headlineQuote: A young player cannot learn a paid craft from an empty bench.
portrait: At **43**, Lena is an experienced organist with a music bachelor’s degree, two children, a mortgage and three weeks saved.
Her partner’s **variable delivery hours** and low local fees make even AI Plateau anxious.
She avoids **AI tools** and relies on written paid rotas, pupils and properly funded apprenticeships.
Across AGI dates, she protects **chapel and teaching pay** and considers school posts only with real net gains.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase arrangements and reduce chapel fees before Lena secures suitable school hours.
whatWouldHelp: **Written paid dates**, a suitable tutor opening and lender help before arrears would protect the mortgage.
